title: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
one_liner: Pick a small training subset that covers important and varied web actions, then trim page state around the true target so offline web-agent training becomes cheaper and transfers better.
lead: Offline web-agent training often wastes compute on repeated trajectories, repeated websites, and large page-state dumps that do not help the next action because they repeat the same signal or add irrelevant page detail. Weasel attacks that waste directly. It selects a fixed-budget subset of steps that are both important and varied, then prunes page state around the action target so training focuses on what matters for the decision.

problem.h2: Why more web data is not always better
paras: Web-agent datasets can be huge, but much of that size comes from near-duplicate steps and very long page-state descriptions. Training on everything is expensive, and the extra examples may not teach much because the agent sees the same patterns again and again.

The problem is worse out of domain. If training data is concentrated on a few sites or a few interaction styles, the agent may memorize those habits and then fail on new sites because it never learned a broader set of action patterns.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Spend the training budget on steps that are both important and diverse, and trim each page state around the true action target.

panels.title: 2. Choose important steps

Compare steps across sites, states, and interaction patterns so that the chosen subset is not full of near-duplicates.
Use a greedy method to keep the examples with the best combined importance and diversity score.

steps.b: Prune page state near the target action
steps.text: Keep content around the true target so that the model sees the most relevant part of the page.

steps.text: Replace expert traces with model-style rationales where needed so that the training text better matches how the model reasons during use.

paras: The paper changes which training examples the agent sees and how much page state is attached to each example. That matters because the training budget is fixed, so each retained example should carry more useful information.
object.object: the offline training set for web-agent fine-tuning

hidden.name: how much useful coverage each chosen step adds
paras: The key hidden quantity is the marginal value of one more training step. A step is useful if it teaches an important decision that the current subset does not already cover. That value is hidden because you only discover it after comparing the step against many others.

Weasel estimates that hidden value through importance and diversity. A step should be kept when it teaches a strong decision and adds a new pattern, because either factor alone is not enough for good transfer.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark examples that add more useful coverage to a fixed-size training subset.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is how much a candidate training step teaches beyond what the current subset already teaches.
The selection rule balances unary importance with pairwise diversity so that the final subset is both strong and broad.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: spend compute on broader signal, not repeated clutter
paras: If you train on many duplicated web steps, the model spends a large share of its budget rehearsing the same decision. That can still lower training loss, but it does not broaden what the agent knows how to do. A fixed-size subset that covers more decision types is more useful because the agent sees a wider range of actions per unit of compute.

The page-state pruning rule helps for a separate reason because web page descriptions can be long and much of that text is unrelated to the next action. By keeping content near the true target, Weasel lowers the amount of irrelevant text the model must read, so training is cheaper and the action signal is less diluted.

stages.s: Prune page state around the target
A smaller training set with better transfer because it covers more useful patterns per unit of compute

math.h2: Select the subset with the best combined value
math.words: One compact summary is to score a chosen subset by adding the importance of each kept step and the diversity gained from keeping different kinds of steps together.
symbols: overall value of the chosen training subset S
how broadly the subset covers different sites, states, and action patterns
weight on the diversity part of the score

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Subset A keeps three highly repeated checkout steps with total importance 9 and diversity 1.
Subset B keeps one checkout step, one search step, and one form step with total importance 8 and diversity 4.
The method chooses Subset B because it gives nearly the same importance and much broader coverage.

math.note: The paper uses a more detailed objective and a greedy solver, but this equation captures the main tradeoff.

charts.title: Standard full-data fine-tuning
charts.note: Training on everything is slow and repetitive, so the compute budget is spent on many low-value examples.

charts.title: Weasel
charts.note: The paper reports better transfer with large speedups because the selected subset carries more useful signal and less clutter.

items.html: If the scoring rule underestimates a subtle but important step, the subset may lose a case that matters for later transfer.

items.b: Too much pruning can hide context.
items.html: Keeping only the target neighborhood may remove page cues that explain why that target is correct, so the agent may learn a brittle local rule.

items.b: Style matching can narrow the explanation range.
items.html: Replacing expert rationales with model-style rationales may fit the current model better because the training text matches the model's usual style, but it can also reduce exposure to richer human explanations.
The method is useful because it treats data selection as a core part of web-agent training rather than an afterthought.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Take a medium-size offline web dataset and train two agents with the same compute budget. The first uses the full set in chronological order. The second uses Weasel's fixed-budget subset plus target-centered page-state pruning. Evaluate both on new sites and on sites seen during training.

The demo should show that the Weasel agent transfers better to new sites because its training set covers more varied useful patterns. Report training time and average page-state length so that the cost savings are visible too.
demo.metric_eq: transfer_gain = score_new_sites_weasel - score_new_sites_full ; time_drop = train_time_full - train_time_weasel
demo.closing: The core claim is that a smaller sharper dataset can beat a larger noisier one.
